title: Fragment reclamation credit scheduler and kernel warmup propagation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: paged attention workloads experience uneven KV fragment churn across tenants. On load spikes we see knee-ingests: prefill latency spikes and decode stalls when fragmented segments are rehydrated. Existing eviction heuristics (LRU-like) create oscillation for hot-but-intermittent fragments and cause repeated kernel cold-starts.

Proposal: implement a Fragment Reclamation Credit Scheduler (FRCS) plus Kernel Warmup Propagation (KWP). FRCS assigns reclaim credits to fragments based on multi-factor score (recent touch frequency, tenant weight, predicted reuse from workload heatmap, and kernel affinity). Credits act as guarded soft-residency: fragments with >threshold credits are protected from eviction and prioritized for contiguous placement. KWP piggybacks warmup signals from chosen kernel variants: when a kernel path is selected (e.g., fused attention kernel), KWP triggers speculative lightweight prefill for adjacent fragments that the heatmap predicts will be used within the next N tokens, avoiding full decode but warming allocator/kernel caches and KV bloom overlays.
acceptance_criteria: 1) FRCS implemented as a pluggable allocator component with per-fragment credit ledger and eviction hooks
2) KWP provides speculative prefill path that reduces first-token decode latency for predicted fragments by >=20% on benchmark suites
3) End-to-end regression: p99 prefill latency does not increase >5% and overall token cost per request decreases or stays flat for 95% of workloads
4) Multi-tenant fairness: tenants with equal weights see <10% variance in tail decode stalls after rollout
5) Feature guarded behind runtime flag and can be rolled-back per-pool
6) Unit and integration tests added; e2e benchmark and A/B dashboard available in Console
notes: Key idea: avoid binary resident/non-resident semantics by adding a time-decaying credit that expresses short-term reuse potential. Combine with a lightweight bloom overlay so KWP can decide whether speculative prefill is cheap. Credits are charged and refunded during sequencing and soft-evict operations to prevent long-term hoarding.
implementation_summary: Phase 1: credit ledger + eviction hook + metrics (4w). Phase 2: KWP speculative prefill prototype with heatmap predictor and bloom overlay (3w). Phase 3: integration, QA, rollout flags and dashboards (2w). Implementation will live in runtime/allocator with an API for kernel adapters to register warmup hints.
metrics_and_observability: Add metrics: fragment_credit_balance, speculative_prefill_count, speculative_prefill_success_rate, kv_rehydrate_time_p50_p95_p99, decode_stall_rate, tenant_prefill_cost_by_weight. Add per-pool dashboard and A/B compare against control.
test_plan: Unit tests for ledger accrual/decay and eviction determinism. Integration test with synthetic workloads that simulate bursty conversational sessions and streaming generation. e2e benchmark using bench-suite-v2: measure p50/p95/p99 prefill latency, token cost delta, and KV hit-rate. Canary rollout at 5% traffic in runtime-1.20 followed by 25%/100% if metrics look good.
tradeoffs: Pros: reduces cold-kernel impact, improves tail latency for hot-but-sparse fragments, better multi-tenant fairness. Cons: added allocator complexity, potential for credit accumulation to favor heavy tenants unless weights enforced, small additional CPU for bloom maintenance and heatmap scoring. We will mitigate by weight caps, decay windows, and guardrails in canary.
risks: Risk of increased memory overhead from speculative warmups and bloom overlays; risk of mispredictions increasing token cost; possible interactions with existing compaction/defrag passes. Contention on credit ledger updates under very high QPS requires lock-free design or sharding.
open_questions: What is the best decay half-life for credits across conversational vs. batching workloads?
Should speculative prefill produce partial KV frames (cheap) or full decoded prefills (expensive) initially?
How to surface credit balances and heatmap feedback to customers (if at all)?
Blocker: dependency on compacted-page API changes proposed in ENG-61234 — will need alignment
decisions: We will implement time-decaying credits with a configurable half-life defaulting to 30s for conversational flows and 300s for long-batch flows. Speculative prefill will start with lightweight bloom-based overlay updates (no full token decode) and be expanded to partial-decode warmups if safe. Credits are tenant-weighted with an enforced cap proportional to pool size.
